title: Fibonacci Solution
summary: Walks through turning the Fibonacci flowchart into code: base cases with if / else if, a hand-written sum of the last two items, then replacing the repetition with a for loop that uses output.length for the last two positions.

concepts.heading: Step 1: base cases from the flowchart
points: Create output as an empty array inside the function.
else if (n === 2) set output to [0, 1]. An else if is only evaluated when the earlier condition was false.
else branch handles every larger n: start output at [0, 1], then add more terms.
All branches fall through to a single return output at the end.

concepts.heading: Step 2: first manual sum
points: Inside else, the next number is output[0] + output[1] (0 + 1 = 1) and is appended with output.push(...); the array becomes [0, 1, 1].
The flowchart then asks whether n equals the array's length; if yes return, otherwise add again. This suggests an if (n === output.length) check.

concepts.heading: Step 3: make the indexes dynamic
points: Hard-coded positions 0 and 1 only work for a two-item array. Use output.length - 1 for the last item and output.length - 2 for the second last; this works at any size (length 4 gives positions 3 and 2).
length is a property, so no parentheses (the lecture's spoken output.length() is loose wording).

concepts.heading: Step 4: collapse the repetition into a loop
points: Repeated lines plus the 'go back and check again' arrow are the signal to use a loop.
for loop: counter starts at 2 (two items already exist), condition i < n, step i++. Each round pushes the sum of the last two items.
The loop ends when i reaches n, which leaves exactly n items. The loop condition replaces the explicit length-vs-n check.
Test with n = 1, 2 and 5 in the sandbox, then run the course checker.

concepts.heading: Closing advice
points: Many routes work (while loop, fewer if branches); correct output meeting the stated rules is what counts, and the best solution is one the learner understands.
Common sticking points flagged: array methods and remembering to loop.

task.name: Fibonacci solution walkthrough
task.starting_point: fibonacciGenerator(n) stub from the previous lecture.
task.goal: Return the first n numbers of the sequence as an array.
steps: if n is 1 return [0] via output; else if n is 2 use [0, 1].
Loop i from 2 while i < n.
In each round push output[output.length-1] + output[output.length-2].
Run with n = 1, 2, 5, then use the checker.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 15 - Intermediate Javascript/15.13 - Introducing the Fibonacci Code Challenge/script.js

pitfalls: Writing output.length() with parentheses (it is a property).
Starting the loop at 0 or 1 so the first terms get duplicated.
Using <= n and getting n+1 items.
(Extra) n = 0 or negative: the lecture's code returns [0, 1] for n = 0; add an explicit guard if needed.
Reference repo diverges: it uses a different but valid single-loop structure.

playground.coverage: Solution uses early returns for 0 and 1, loops from index 2 pushing output[i-1]+output[i-2], plus a rolling-variables alternative. Notes explain edge cases and loop start.
gaps_and_ideas: Add the lecture's progression (manual sum, then dynamic indexes with length, then the loop) as an incremental walkthrough.
